# Intro to Geometry Nodes — transformations and CSG

[Transformations and CSG]({{ site.baseurl }}/sessions/#b02) · Target weeks 2

Build the instructor's three-operation CSG example from native primitives and rotated cylinders.

Use these example files only as a reference if you are struggling with a step. Build your own file and follow the process one step at a time. Compare the example to understand where you are stuck, then return to your own work. The supplied examples are not files to submit as your assignment.

Select the lesson object and change parameters on the nodes or, where provided, in the GeometryNodes modifier. Press Home over the node editor. Explanations are in Frames and native node names are retained. Build the exercise in a new file of your own, following each step in order.

## Example files and steps

**[Intro to Geometry Nodes — transformations and CSG]({{ site.baseurl }}/files/blender/01-intro-geometry-nodes/Intro-Geometry-Nodes.blend)**

1. 01 - CSG example

The instructor's graph uses Intersection, rotated cylinders, Union and Difference. Read the Frames in order. Change Radius, Size, Translation, Rotation or Scale on the native nodes; these controls are not in the modifier.

## Short assignment

Make three variants by changing one parameter at a time. Diagram Intersection, Union and Difference in the order used.

## Lesson notes and project connection

[Transformations and CSG]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/tutorials/u02-transformations-and-csg/) — In the next unit, replace a primitive Boolean cutter with geometry built from points and faces.

Develop this exercise in [P1 — Geometry — from operations to construction]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/assignments/p1-geometry-from-operations-to-construction/).
